html:
Muteesa I was the kabaka, or king, of Buganda from 1856 until his death in 1884, ruling the strongest state on the northern shore of Lake Victoria.

He ran a large court of chiefs and pages and a fleet of war canoes. He welcomed Swahili and Arab traders from the coast and for some years kept the fast of Ramadan, the first great opening of Buganda to Islam.

He received the explorer Speke in 1862 and Stanley in 1875, whose letter inviting missionaries brought Anglicans in 1877 and Catholics in 1879. He played the three faiths against each other and against Egyptian pressure from the north. Under his son Mwanga, rivalry among them led to the killing of the Uganda Martyrs and to civil war.
sum: Muteesa I was the kabaka, or king, of Buganda from 1856 until his death in 1884, ruling the strongest state on the northern shore of Lake Victoria.
